h1: The Park Nangrong Resort — a quiet garden resort that makes a budget-friendly Phanom Rung base
intro: If you want to stay close to Phanom Rung without bedding down in Buriram city, which is further away — The Park Nangrong Resort is a name that comes up often in reviews from Khmer-temple travelers. It is a small 3-star resort of 24 rooms in Nang Rong District, by Nong Ta Moo pond, decorated in a modern resort style with leafy gardens and a quiet, family-run feel. Rooms start from about THB 650/night with a score of 8.5. The draw is that it is clean, quiet and remarkably easy on the wallet for a Phanom Rung base.

body.html: The Park Nangrong Resort's selling point is its location in Nang Rong District, on Praditpana Road by Nong Ta Moo pond — just a few minutes from Nang Rong town and about 25–30 km from the Phanom Rung and Prasat Muang Tam Khmer temples, roughly a half-hour drive on. For anyone planning an early start to catch the sunrise aligning through the Phanom Rung gateway, or hopping between Khmer temples in a single day, staying in Nang Rong trims a lot of the drive you would face from Buriram city, which sits much further away.

The resort is a low-rise property in a modern resort style, wrapped in gardens and greenery that give it a private feel. There are 24 rooms, each with air-conditioning, a TV, a fridge, a hot shower and free Wi-Fi. Choices range from Deluxe double and twin rooms to villa-style units. What guests praise most is that the rooms are clean and well kept and the surroundings are quiet and leafy — exactly what you want for a good night's sleep after a day of driving between temples.
"Clean, peaceful place with a lovely garden. The owners and staff are warm, almost like staying with relatives. Excellent value for visiting Phanom Rung."

That family-run atmosphere comes up again and again — the owners run it themselves, the staff are friendly, and they happily point you toward the temples and to places to eat in Nang Rong. There is a small on-site restaurant and a Thai breakfast that several guests describe as tasty and filling for the price. Free parking, pet-friendly rooms and a 24-hour front desk round it out. For an out-of-town resort in the budget bracket, what you get is genuinely enough for everyday use.

Things to know before you book: a number of real reviews note that the entrance to the resort is fairly narrow and poorly lit, and tricky to find on a first visit, especially after dark — keep your GPS on and call ahead. Wi-Fi can be patchy in some rooms. The mattresses are on the firm side for some tastes, and staff speak limited English, so international visitors may want a translation app handy.

The other thing to weigh up is getting around. This place suits people driving themselves or renting a car, since it is out of the main town and public transport is not convenient, with most evening dining options back in Nang Rong town. And if your main reason for coming is football at Chang Arena or racing at Chang International Circuit, note that it sits about 50 km from Buriram city, so allow a fair bit of driving time on event days.

Overall it is a small resort that does the job of a Phanom Rung base very well at a very light price — clean rooms, leafy gardens, a quiet setting and warm, hands-on hosts, all closer to the Khmer temple cluster than the city. The 8.5 score reflects that most guests leave happy with the value. If you can live with a hard-to-find entrance, firmish beds and Wi-Fi that is not strong everywhere, this is a worthwhile pick for budget-minded temple and history travelers.

faqTitle: FAQ — The Park Nangrong Resort, Nang Rong

faq.q: Where is The Park Nangrong Resort and how far is it from Phanom Rung?
faq.a: It is at 445/10 Praditpana Road, Nang Rong District, Buriram Province, by Nong Ta Moo pond, about 2 km from Nang Rong town. It is roughly 25–30 km from Phanom Rung and Prasat Muang Tam, about a 30-minute drive, and about 50 km from Buriram city.

faq.q: How much does The Park Nangrong Resort cost and what rooms are there?
faq.a: Prices start at about THB 650/night for a Deluxe room. Options range from Deluxe double and twin rooms to villa-style units and a Family Room. Every room has air-con, TV, fridge, hot shower and free Wi-Fi. Rates vary by date, so compare a few platforms before booking.

faq.q: Is it good for visiting Phanom Rung?
faq.a: Very much so. It is a resort in Nang Rong District, closer to the Khmer temple cluster than Buriram city. It is about a 30-minute drive to Phanom Rung — ideal for an early start to see the sunrise through the gateway or to take in Prasat Muang Tam in the same day, all on a budget.

faq.q: Is it good for watching events at Chang Arena?
faq.a: Not ideal if events are your focus. The resort is in Nang Rong District, about 50 km from Chang Arena and Buriram city, so it means a long drive on event days. If you are mainly here for football or racing, a hotel near the stadium is more convenient — but for temple trips, this location works better.

faq.q: What should I watch out for before booking?
faq.a: Real reviews note that the entrance is fairly narrow and dark and hard to find on a first visit, especially at night. Wi-Fi can be patchy in some rooms, mattresses are on the firm side for some tastes, and staff speak limited English. Keep your GPS accurate and call ahead for directions.

faq.q: What parking and facilities are there?
faq.a: There is free parking, ideal for driving around the temples. The resort has an on-site restaurant, a Thai breakfast, leafy gardens, a 24-hour front desk, laundry service, and is pet-friendly. Free Wi-Fi is available in all rooms.
